This draft covers WF3 steps 1-9 for D-002 (Atlas Growth Fund I LP; record date 2026-12-15; payment date 2027-01-12; USD 8,000,000; one component, D-002-A, a US-source dividend from Orion Manufacturing Inc. paid through Atlas Acquisition SPV LLC, which is disregarded; DOC-0202). Steps 10-12 are still open: second review by someone other than the preparer, sign-off, release, and the withholding record. I have read-only access, so nothing was written to clearance.withholding_schedule or withholding_determination, no case was opened and no cure was started. The tax team needs to do these.

RECONCILIATION (C3.4): Gross is 8,000,000, which matches the notice and the sum of the 12 distribution_lines. Each line equals unit_pct x 8,000,000. Tax withheld is 1,125,900. Net is 6,874,100. The two transparent payees are paid in aggregate: CP-102 (Atlas Lux Feeder SCSp) gets gross 1,920,000, tax 384,000, net 1,536,000. CP-107 (Sterling Nominees) gets gross 480,000, tax 144,000, net 336,000.

KEY POINTS FOR THE REVIEWER:
1. Rate version: payment falls in 2027, so the Luxembourg treaty rate is R-02 v2027.1 at 10%, not v2026.1 at 15%. In the rulebook, R-02 v2026.1 still has eff_to = null; it should be closed at 2026-12-31.
2. R-03 at 5% is applied only to I-003, whose effective vote in Orion is exactly 10.0% (12.5% x 80%). Please confirm that "at least 10%" is met and that holding the votes through the fund partnership and the disregarded SPV qualifies. I-004 (9.99%), I-005 (8%: its Class B units carry 13% economic interest but 10% of the vote) and I-010 (9.6%) all fall below the threshold.
3. I-013 (Echternach Pension Fund, behind Sterling): form F-013 expires 2026-12-31, before the payment date (scenario S3.5). It needs a WF2 renewal with 2027-01-12 as the deadline. There is also a discrepancy: the Sterling withholding statement (DOC-0107) cites an Echternach W-8BEN-E dated 4 March 2025, and TS-013 starts on 2025-03-04, but tax_form only holds F-013, signed 2023-03-06. A newer valid form may already exist. If so, the line can be cleared at 10% (tax 30,000 instead of 90,000).
4. I-011 (Moselle Capital, behind the feeder) moved its seat to Belgium on 2026-12-01. The source notice, DOC-0111, is not digitised, so the residence change rests only on the database record. CL-002 still shows the feeder as fully cleared to 2028, so a WF2 change case is needed for I-011. The rulebook has no US-Belgium rule, so a Belgian treaty rate cannot be applied even with a new form.
5. I-006 (Meridian Holdings I): change case K-006 is still open. The new ownership is circular (I-006 and I-018 each own 30% of the other) and ultimately traces to a Jersey trust. The ownership-based LOB claim is doubtful even on the pre-restructuring facts, since the trust held 100%. I defaulted to 30% until K-006 is resolved.
6. Defaults are I-011, I-006, I-013, I-014 and I-015. Under C3.7, investor relations must notify each before payment with the item needed: a Belgian-residence W-8BEN-E (I-011), resolution of K-006 with an updated ownership chain and LOB (I-006), a renewed W-8BEN-E (I-013), beneficial-owner documentation through Sterling (I-014), and a new W-8BEN-E (I-015).
7. Holds were not used: the LPA (DOC-0001) is not digitised, so I could not confirm the fund's terms allow a hold.
8. I-008 and I-009 are both named "Alpha Holdings SA" but are different entities (Luxembourg vs Switzerland). They are kept separate.
9. I-012 (France) and I-009 (Switzerland) are at 30% because their forms make no treaty claim. This is a documented choice, but investor relations may want to tell them they could claim a treaty rate.
10. Data timing: the system date is 2026-10-14, but several inputs are dated later (notice DOC-0202 on 2026-12-07, I-011 residence record entered 2026-12-20, payment P-010 on 2026-12-04). Please confirm these are the right as-at facts before sign-off. The pension-fund exemption under the real US-Luxembourg treaty is not modelled in the rulebook, so I-001 is at 10% under R-02."}
